assign.outcome:
**Site diff lands** — one command that shoots the site before and after a landing and says what changed, so the owner stops finding breaks one page at a time.

`node public/framework/ext/DesignTool/diff/site-diff.mjs baseline --out <dir>` shoots 40 representative pages (one of each kind: realms, paging, layouts, blog, notes, platform, size/spacing/controls) at 1280 and 3440, saves a PNG per page-per-width plus `manifest.json`.
`node site-diff.mjs compare --baseline <dir> --out <dir>` re-shoots the SAME set (read out of the baseline's own manifest) and reports pixels changed, new console errors, new sideways scroll — worst page first — in `report.json` and a stdout table. Exits non-zero only when something got worse.

The framework's live clock (`.panel-t-clock`) is painted flat grey before every shot on both sides, so it never shows as "changed".

Self-test against the shared server: baseline 40×2 in 13.1s, 0 console errors. Compare against itself: 0 of 40 pages changed (the mask holds pixel-exact, even on the clock's own page), 18.4s. Compare with `--inject "a{text-decoration:underline!important}"`: 40 of 40 changed, correctly ranked — the link-heaviest pages (paging library, blog front, home) land at the top, the link-lightest (design/size, design/controls) at the bottom. 19.8s. Both real runs are well under the 90s budget.

log.msg: root cause found: this is NOT a shared-Page bug (the new per-page inFlight assertion never fired) - it is a real Playwright/Chromium race when two DISTINCT Page objects call goto() at nearly the same instant (confirmed reproducing even after switching to sequential page creation + strict per-slot ownership). Fix: serialize just the goto() call across the whole run with a tiny async lock, leaving the rest of each shot (evaluate/screenshot/waitForTimeout) concurrent.

fixed: serialGoto() lock around page.goto() only (rest of a shot stays concurrent across the 4-page pool) - eliminated the Playwright cross-navigation error entirely. Verified: 2 fresh baseline runs post-fix, 160 total shots, 0 errored, 0 missing files (vs 24-of-40 erroring before the fix). Also fixed: errored/missing shots now report changed:"unknown", sort to the top of the table, add an "(N unknown - shot errored)" clause to the summary line, and fail the exit code - verified live in the pre-fix run (24 unknown, exit 1). Residual note: a compare run showed 28/40 pages changed - confirmed NOT a bug: framework/styles/layers/theme/lew42/lew42.css (a shared theme file) was edited by another concurrent agent mid-test (mtime confirmed) - the tool correctly caught a real site-wide change in flight.

assign.outcome:
**Fix landed** — the coordinator's real `compare` run hit `page.goto: Navigation to X is interrupted by another navigation to Y` on several `styles/layouts/*` shots at 3440. Root cause: NOT a shared-Page bug (the pool already gave every url its own Page for its whole goto→settle→shoot lifecycle, and the new per-page ownership assertion never fired) — it's Chromium/Playwright itself cross-wiring two DIFFERENT Page objects when their `.goto()` calls start at nearly the same instant. Fix: `serialGoto()` wraps only the `.goto()` call in a tiny async lock, browser-wide — waiting for fonts, masking and screenshotting still run concurrently across the 4-page pool.

Verified: 2 fresh baseline+compare pairs after the fix, 160 total shots, 0 errored, 0 missing files (vs 24-of-40 erroring before the fix, reproduced once for confirmation). Also fixed: an errored/missing shot now reports `changed: "unknown"`, sorts to the top of the table, adds a `(N unknown — shot errored)` clause to the summary line, and fails the exit code — all verified live in the pre-fix run (24 unknown, exit 1).

One compare run afterward showed 28 of 40 pages 'changed' — checked and it is NOT a regression: `framework/styles/layers/theme/lew42/lew42.css`, a shared theme file, was edited by another concurrent agent mid-test (its mtime falls inside the test window) — the tool correctly caught a real, live site-wide change in flight, which is exactly its job.
